turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select
the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The second-order NLO susceptibility (and thus \(|d_{ij}|\)) vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal and is also identically zero in point group 432. Consequently only non-centrosymmetric candidates can appear in the top five. Among the allowed structures the magnitude of \(d_{ij}\) is governed by Miller’s rule (\(d\sim\chi^{(1)3}\)) together with the degree of polar alignment of the hyperpolarizable bonds. This immediately selects covalent, tetrahedrally bonded networks that contain the heaviest, most polarizable atoms (As, Te, I) and that possess the smallest gaps.

- c055 is a 6H-type polytype of (Al,Ga)As. The local bonding is identical to zinc-blende GaAs (\(d_{14}\approx90{-}170\) pm V\(^{-1}\)); the polar space group \(P6_3mc\) converts this into a comparably large \(d_{33}\).
- c030 is the chalcopyrite CdSiP\(_2\) (I\(\bar{4}2d\)), a well-documented IR NLO crystal with measured \(d_{36}=84.5\) pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c073 is a low-symmetry (effectively \(P1\)) ordered substitution of the CdTe/InAs/In\(_2\)Te\(_3\) family. All cations remain tetrahedral, the average gap is smaller than that of CdSiP\(_2\), and every \(d_{ij}\) component is allowed, producing an even larger tensor.
- c070 adopts the sulvanite structure (P\(\bar{4}3m\)) of Cu\(_3\)TaTe\(_4\). Both Cu and Ta sit in Te\(_4\) tetrahedra; the heavy Te atoms and modest gap yield a large \(d_{14}\).
- c039 (RbGeI\(_3\)) contains stereochemically active Ge\(^{2+}\) lone pairs and highly polarizable iodide. The resulting one-dimensional polar chains give a giant static hyperpolarizability, placing its leading \(d_{ij}\) in the same range as the tetrahedral arsenides/tellurides.

All other candidates are either centrosymmetric, possess lighter anions (S, Se, Cl, Br), or exhibit partial cancellation of the local dipoles, and therefore have distinctly smaller \(|d_{ij}|\).

Final: c055, c030, c073, c070, c039
